paragraphs: R’ Yonatan (the colleague of R’ Evyatar).

Hyman describes him as R’ Yochanan’s student, reporting in his name in Bereshit Rabbah 64:4. In Hyman’s account, cited as Gittin 36a, R’ Yochanan entrusts the matter to R’ Chiyya bar Abba, followed by a question whether anything further is needed and the reply, “You need nothing further.” In Gittin 6b, R’ Evyatar sends a message to Rav Chisda. Later in the passage, R’ Evyatar says that he found a fly with her, and R’ Yonatan says that he found a hair. R’ Evyatar meets Elijah and asks what the Holy One, blessed be He, is doing. Elijah replies, “My son Evyatar says this; My son Yonatan says that,” etc. Bereshit Rabbah 9:5 mentions R’ Chiyya, the son of R’ Berekhiah’s daughter, and R’ Yonatan replies to him, etc.

notes.text: Hyman’s Gittin 36a summary leaves the speaker of the question compressed; the bounded check did not establish the named episode. The fly and hair are the two reported explanations, not an Aramaic “let us say.”

No new primary scalar was returned. The earlier bounded Gittin 36a search did not locate the exchange; this is not global absence, an alternative-folio finding or speaker adjudication. לא צריכת is SECOND PERSON, YOU do not need, not I do not need. The compressed question/answer interlocutors remain unspecified. נימא is a HAIR, not let us say; the fly and hair are alternative explanations, not combined events. Chiyya is Berekhiah’s DAUGHTER’S SON. Hyman owns the disciple and colleague characterizations. Bereshit 64:4 and 9:5 are contextual readings beside the supplied locators, not 84:4/89:5; no fresh whole chapters are claimed. All personal-title abbreviations remain R-prime except source full Rav Chisda, which is preserved.

Hyman’s print gives Gittin 36a and names Yochanan. The corresponding prosbol exchange in the consulted Gittin 37a:6 and Rashba names Yonatan as the transmitter to Chiyya bar Abba. In the Davidson translation Yonatan asks, “Do I need anything else?” and Chiyya answers, “You do not need anything else.” In Gittin 6b, Evyatar’s message to Rav Chisda concerns divorce documents. The later discussion gives Evyatar’s fly and Yonatan’s hair, and Elijah’s explanation accounts for both. The consulted Bereshit Rabbah 64:4 has Yonatan reporting in Yochanan’s name. At 9:5 Yonatan addresses Chiyya, the son of Berekhiah’s daughter. The passages preserve local attributions; the biographical characterization is Hyman’s.
